distinguishing_features: Adds discrete passive high-density point masses to the span midpoint to lower natural frequency below the shedding frequency
Breaks VIV lock-in by detuning the frequency ratio fn/fs < 0.8 without damping or wall-thickness change
Uses only already-recorded flow_rate and pressure to validate the intervention
Physical hardware design change rather than a monitoring/inference or operational-limit scheme
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to suppress vortex-induced vibration fatigue on an existing subsea pipeline span by shifting its structural natural frequency out of the lock-in band without adding damping, changing wall thickness, or installing new instrumentation.
parsed.viable_reason: The detuning-beyond-lock-in physics is unsound as written: mass loading necessarily requires attaching heavy blocks to an unmodified operating subsea pipe, requires ~2.8x effective-mass increase that is not shown feasible, and the pass/fail test relies on pressure-fluctuation proxy that cannot reliably detect vibration amplitude, so the mechanism is not credibly validated at the stated scale.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Adding discrete mass to a span to detune its natural frequency away from a known excitation frequency is elementary structural-dynamics practice, so the distinguishing feature is an obvious routine step once the failure is recognized.
